prompt.context: Your client is Keep-It-Fresh, a leading fresh fruit and vegetable wholesaler based in Atlanta, GA. Keep-it-Fresh has recently been acquired by a major impact investor, and has been asked by the new owner to improve its sustainability profile. Keep-it-Fresh is a vertically integrated wholesaler that operates farms and sells its fresh products to professional clients: supermarkets, restaurants, and hotels. It is a top 3 US fresh produce wholesaler with annual revenue of $300M. Keep-it-Fresh already enforces best-in-class social practices (wages, paid overtime, health insurance, etc.), but nothing is done in terms of environmental sustainability. The new owner wants to maintain good financial returns but is also concerned about the environmental and social footprint of its investment. The investor expects any sustainability plan to be implemented and show positive impact as soon as possible.
prompt.question: The CEO of Keep-it-Fresh has asked your team to identify the key sustainability issues the company should be working on.

clarifying_info.q: What does produce waste refer to?
clarifying_info.a: Produce waste refers to fresh fruits and vegetables lost, either during storage and transportation, or unsold.
CO2 emissions are for the entire value chain: farming, storage, and distribution.

Sustainability rating measures the social and environmental impact of the proposed project (jobs created, number of beneficiaries, CO2 emissions avoided, etc.). The methodology behind the ratings is not relevant for this case.

clarifying_info.q: What is the relationship between preparation time and roll-out time units?
clarifying_info.a: A month is 4 weeks. Preparation time is in weeks; roll-out time is in months.

exhibits.title: Keep-it-Fresh's Materiality Map
exhibits.shows: A 2x2 materiality map plotting six sustainability issues on two axes: 'Level of Stakeholders' Concern (external)' (Low to High, x-axis) and 'Current or Potential Impact on Business (internal)' (Low to High, y-axis). Issues are labeled A through F.

axes.x: Level of Stakeholders' Concern (external): Low to High
axes.y: Current or Potential Impact on Business (internal): Low to High

exhibits.title: Sustainability Projects Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing five sustainability projects across four dimensions: Sustainability Rating, NPV (in $M), Preparation time (weeks), and Roll-out time (months). Preparation time is the time needed to assemble a team, find partners, check legal requirements, and make budget available. Roll-out time is the time needed to see the first positive effect of the project.

projects.name: Project 2: Donate unwanted fruits and vegetables to non-profits
Project 3: Market misfit fruits and vegetables to avoid waste
Project 5: Use unsold fruits and vegetables as compost

framework: Farming: crop type (organic/GMO, climate resistance), water usage and sources, groundwater pollution, pesticide and fertilizer use, land pollution
Storage & Warehousing: energy usage (electricity, refrigeration), produce waste from ineffective storage
Sales & Distribution: transportation fuel consumption and atmospheric emissions, in-truck refrigeration efficiency, lost sales from unsold/misfit produce or incorrect orders
Other Stakeholders: environmental regulations around pesticides, crops, and emissions; activist and NGO concern for agriculture

questions.prompt: After presenting your framework, the interviewer hands you Exhibit 1 (Materiality Map). Which sustainability issues are most material for Keep-it-Fresh, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should read the 2x2 correctly: issues in the top-right corner are highest priority (high stakeholder concern AND high business impact). Basic insight: Pesticide usage (F) and Produce waste (C) are the most important issues — both score high on both axes. Second-order insight: CO2 emissions (A) and Groundwater pollution (B) are also material but secondary; candidate should note the priority order. Climate-resisting crops (D) and Water usage (E) are lower priority. Candidate should recognize that 'materiality' combines both external stakeholder concern and internal business impact.

questions.prompt: The CEO agrees to focus on Pesticide usage and Produce waste. Brainstorm how Keep-it-Fresh can reduce pesticide usage in its farms and limit produce waste across its value chain. After brainstorming, the interviewer hands you Exhibit 2. Which project would you advise Keep-it-Fresh to implement?
questions.guidance: Candidate should evaluate the five projects using three criteria: NPV, timeframe (preparation + roll-out), and sustainability rating — while keeping in mind the investor's desire for results ASAP. Step 1: Eliminate Project 2 immediately (negative NPV of -$6M). Step 2: Project 4 has high sustainability rating but low NPV ($2M) and the longest total timeframe (20 weeks prep + 18 months rollout = ~23 months). Step 3: Among Projects 1, 3, and 5 (all medium sustainability rating), compare timeframes and NPV. Project 3 has NPV $5M and total timeframe of 12 weeks + 3 months = ~6 months. Project 5 has NPV $3.5M and total timeframe of 10 weeks + 2 months = ~4.5 months. Project 1 has the highest NPV ($7M) but the longest timeframe (20 weeks + 12 months = ~17 months). Given the ASAP constraint, Project 3 is recommended: it balances strong NPV with a relatively short timeframe. Strong candidates note additional implications of choosing Project 3 (e.g., need to find new distribution channels, potential FDA regulation, client acceptance).

math.setup: Total timeframe = preparation time (convert weeks to months at 4 weeks/month) + roll-out time
steps: Project 1: 20 weeks / 4 = 5 months prep + 12 months rollout = 17 months total, NPV $7M
Project 3: 12 weeks / 4 = 3 months prep + 3 months rollout = 6 months total, NPV $5M
Project 4: 20 weeks / 4 = 5 months prep + 18 months rollout = 23 months total, NPV $2M
Project 5: 10 weeks / 4 = 2.5 months prep + 2 months rollout = 4.5 months total, NPV $3.5M
math.answer: Recommend Project 3 (Market misfit fruits and vegetables): NPV $5M, ~6-month total timeframe, medium sustainability rating — best balance of financial return and speed given investor's ASAP requirement.

brainstorming.prompt: The CEO has decided to focus on Pesticide usage and Produce waste. How can Keep-it-Fresh (1) reduce pesticide usage in its farms, and (2) limit produce waste across its value chain?

categories.name: Reduce pesticide usage
ideas: Use natural/biological pesticides as a substitute for synthetic ones
Forbid usage of the most harmful or regulated pesticides while keeping safer alternatives
Adopt climate-resistant or pest-resistant crop varieties that require fewer pesticides

categories.name: Limit produce waste
ideas: Donate unsold or unwanted produce to non-profit organizations
Smart harvesting techniques to extend produce shelf life after harvesting
Market and sell misfit (cosmetically imperfect) fruits and vegetables instead of discarding
Sell unwanted or surplus produce for animal feed
Improve demand forecasting to reduce over-ordering and unsold inventory
Optimize cold-chain storage and transportation to reduce spoilage

recommendation: Recommend implementing Project 3: Market misfit fruits and vegetables to avoid waste
This project delivers an NPV of $5M and can show positive results within approximately 6 months (12 weeks preparation + 3 months roll-out), satisfying the investor's requirement for rapid impact
Among all viable projects it offers the best combination of financial return and speed
risks: FDA or food safety regulations may restrict the marketing of misfit produce
Risk of cannibalizing current product lines if existing clients switch to lower-priced misfit items
Difficulty convincing current clients (supermarkets, restaurants, hotels) to accept produce they have historically rejected
Challenge of finding new client segments or distribution channels for misfit produce
Consumer/buyer perception that misfit produce is lower quality
next_steps: Size the addressable market for misfit fruits and vegetables
Quantify the volume and variety of misfit produce currently generated by Keep-it-Fresh
Build sales and marketing capacity to target new or existing clients for misfit produce
Review applicable FDA and food safety regulations
Pilot with a small client segment before full roll-out
